record.paper_title: Advances in periodic difference equations with open problems
record.context_brief: Periodic-orbit forcing for periodic interval systems
record.original_question: Let I be a compact interval in the real line, let p be a positive integer, and let f0, …, f_{p-1}: I → I generate the p-periodic non-autonomous system x_{n+1} = f_{n mod p}(x_n). Write Per([f0, …, f_{p-1}]) for the set of least periods of periodic orbits of this system. Characterize the possible sets Per([f0, …, f_{p-1}]) for arbitrary p, extending the exact period-forcing description known for 2-periodic systems.

evidence.quote: For a fixed p ∈ N, consider a p-periodic system defined by the maps [f0, ..., fp−1].
Open Problem 2.1. Extend Theorem 2.1 to periodic sequences of maps of arbitrary period, i.e., characterize the set of periods Per([f0, ..., fp−1]) for any positive integer p.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $I \subset \mathbb{R}$ be a compact interval and let $p$ be a positive integer. Given continuous maps $f_0, f_1, \dots, f_{p-1}: I \to I$, consider the $p$-periodic non-autonomous discrete dynamical system
$$x_{n+1} = f_{n \bmod p}(x_n), \qquad n \ge 0.$$
A point $x \in I$ is called periodic of least period $k$ for this system if $k$ is the smallest positive integer with the property that
$$f_{(k-1) \bmod p} \circ f_{(k-2) \bmod p} \circ \cdots \circ f_{1 \bmod p} \circ f_{0 \bmod p}(x) = x$$
and the corresponding orbit $(x_n)_{n \ge 0}$ has minimal period $k$ as a sequence. Define
$$\mathrm{Per}([f_0, \dots, f_{p-1}]) := \{k \in \mathbb{N} : \text{the system has a periodic orbit of least period } k\}.$$

For $p = 1$, Sharkovsky's theorem completely characterizes the possible sets $\mathrm{Per}(f_0)$: they are exactly the tails of the Sharkovsky order on $\mathbb{N}$ (together with the empty set and certain $2^\infty$-related cases). For $p = 2$, an analogous exact characterization of the possible sets $\mathrm{Per}([f_0, f_1])$ is known.

Problem: For an arbitrary positive integer $p$, give a complete characterization of the family of subsets of $\mathbb{N}$ that arise as $\mathrm{Per}([f_0, \dots, f_{p-1}])$ as $(f_0, \dots, f_{p-1})$ ranges over all $p$-tuples of continuous self-maps of $I$.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open problem in the area of periodic difference equations and remains the subject of active research. Related work (e.g., on alternating systems for $p=2$, folding/unfolding techniques, and spectral invariants for periodic non-autonomous systems by AlSharawi, Cánovas, Linero, and others) has produced partial results, but no general characterization of $\mathrm{Per}([f_0, \dots, f_{p-1}])$ for arbitrary $p$ appears to have been established.

status_evidence.title: Folding and unfolding in periodic difference equations
status_evidence.snippet: Studies set of periods of p-periodic nonautonomous difference equations of continuous interval maps; partial reductions but no full characterization.
status_evidence.claim: The general characterization of period sets for arbitrary p remains open; partial techniques (folding/unfolding) have been developed.

status_evidence.title: Periodic structure of alternating continuous interval maps
status_evidence.snippet: Characterization for the alternating (p=2) case of continuous interval maps.
status_evidence.claim: The exact period-forcing characterization is established for p=2, motivating extensions to arbitrary p.

status_evidence.title: What we need to find out the periods of a periodic difference equation
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses what is required to determine the set of periods of a periodic difference equation.
status_evidence.claim: Determining Per for arbitrary p is treated as an outstanding question.
